dv.title: މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އަލްފާޟިލް މޫސާ ޒަމީރު، ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއްގައި ސްރީލަންކާ އަށް މިއަދު ފުރާވަޑައިގެންފި
dv.description: ސްރީލަންކާ ގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ހިޒް އެކްސެލަންސީ އެމް.ޔޫ.އެމް. ޢަލީ ސަބްރީގެ ދަޢުވަތަކަށް ޖޫން މަހުގެ 03 އިން 06 އަށް ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ސްރީލަންކާގެ ވެރިރަށް ކޮލޮމްބޯ އަށް ވަޑައިގަތުމަށްޓަކައި މިއަދު ފުރާވަޑައިގެންފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
ސްރީލަންކާ ގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ހިޒް އެކްސެލަންސީ އެމް.ޔޫ.އެމް. ޢަލީ ސަބްރީގެ ދަޢުވަތަކަށް ޖޫން މަހުގެ 03 އިން 06 އަށް ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ސްރީލަންކާގެ ވެރިރަށް ކޮލޮމްބޯ އަށް ވަޑައިގަތުމަށްޓަކައި  މިއަދު ފުރާވަޑައިގެންފިއެވެ.

އެ މަނިކުފާނުގެ މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި ސްރީލަންކާގެ ރައީސް ރަނިލް ވިކްރަމަސިންގެ އިތުރުން އެޤައުމުގެ ބޮޑުވަޒީރު، ޑިނޭޝް ގުނަވަރދެނާ އާ ބައްދަލު ކުރެއްވުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. އަދި އެ ޤައުމުގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރާ ބައްދަލުކުރައްވާ ރަސްމީ ވާހަކަތައް ބޭއްވުމަށް ވެސް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. ރަސްމީ ވާހަކަތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި ރާއްޖެއާއި ސްރީލަންކާ އާ ދެމެދު އޮތް ޒަމާންވީ ގުޅުން ފުޅާކުރުމުގެ މަޝްވަރާތައް ކުރިއަށްދާނެއެވެ.

މީގެ އިތުރުން ރާއްޖެއާއި ސްރީލަންކާ އާ ދެމެދު ތަފާތު ދާއިރާތަކުން އޮންނަ ގުޅުންތައް އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމަށް ސަރުކާރުގެ އިސްވެރިންނާއި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ބައްދަލުކުރައްވާ ވާހަކަފުޅު ދެއްކެވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ.

ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުގެ މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި ސްޓޭޓް މިނިސްޓަރު ޝެރީނާ އަބްދުއްސަމަދު، އެޑިޝަނަލް ސެކްރެޓަރީ ޝިރުޒިމަތު ސަމީރު އަދި ޑިރެކްޓަރ-ޖެނެރަލް އައިޝަތު ފަރީނާ ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވައެވެ.

en.title: Maldives - EU: 5th Senior Officials Meeting takes place in Malé
en.description: The Fifth Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union (EU) was held on 2 June 2024 in Malé, Maldives.
en.body:
The Fifth Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and the European Union (EU) was held on 2 June 2024 in Malé, Maldives.

The Maldives and the EU confirmed their mutual interest to further strengthen and deepen the mutually beneficial cooperation rooted in shared values and commitment to the principles of the UN Charter and international law. The Maldives and the EU reaffirmed their commitment to cooperate in various sectors, including democratic reforms, the green transition, climate change mitigation and adaptation, good governance, human rights, and security.

The EU congratulated the Maldives on the well organised major elections, the Presidential Elections held in September 2023 and the Parliamentary elections held in April 2024. The Maldives thanked the EU for sending an Elections Observation Mission (EOM) during the Presidential election and welcomed the final report. The EU and the Maldives discussed that the implementation of the recommendations received in the EOM report would further strengthen the electoral process and help consolidate democracy in the Maldives.

As a result of the Maldives’ membership of the Organization of African, Caribbean, and Pacific States (OACPS), the Maldives is currently in the process of completing the domestic legal procedures to sign and ratify the Samoa Agreement. This is a step towards enhancing the relationship between the Maldives and the European Union, as well as towards regional integration. It is a precursor for the Maldives to negotiate its accession to an interim Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) between a regional group of OACPS and the EU, which provides for a tariff-free access to the EU market.

During the meeting, the Maldives also focused on the ongoing initiatives to improve the governance system, build economic resilience, strengthen democracy, promote the rule of law and to ensure protection of human rights through implementation of significant changes to the legal and justice sectors. The Maldives also elaborated on plans to integrate human rights protection and promotion into the development strategies, particularly to enhance protections for vulnerable groups, including women, children, and persons with disabilities. The EU and the Maldives emphasised the importance of ensuring space for a vibrant civil society, and upholding freedom of expression and opinion as key foundation of democracy.

The Maldives expressed gratitude to EU for implementing projects on green recovery, good governance, and other various support measures through the EU’s Multi-Annual Indicative Programme (MIP) 2021-2027. In this regard, the Maldives noted with appreciation, the generous assistance through the EU-UNDP partnership agreement “Accountability and Integrity Matters – AIM Project”, valued at EUR 5 million (MVR 74.8 million), aimed at strengthening the rule of law and enhancing transparency and integrity within relevant institutions.

The financing agreement on “Improved Biodiversity Management to support a Blue Economy in the Maldives,” was signed on the sidelines of the Fifth Senior Officials Meeting. This programme of EUR 6.5 million (MVR 97.2 million) under the MIP focused on biodiversity protection and sustainable management of natural resources, which will build the local capacity to manage multiple bioreserve areas.

The Maldives also stressed on the significant challenges in waste management and ensuring energy security and sought support from the EU to establish comprehensive and sustainable waste management solutions and securing funds to develop renewable energy systems capable of providing 33% of the nation’s electrical needs in the next five years. In that regard,

the Maldives expressed appreciation for the ongoing support provided through the Global Gateway strategy notably the Sustainability Energy Development Programme implemented by EIB. This operation is a EUR 45 million EIB loan guaranteed by the EU budget, which enables Maldives to reduce diesel usage and bring down the cost of electricity generation, enhance the use of renewables, provide affordable power to unserved and under-served businesses and residences, and reduce CO2 emissions.

The Maldives recognised other Global Gateway support that increases resilience to pandemics and the efficiency of its health sector with a EUR 18.5 million EIB loan equally covered by an EU guarantee to establish a modern national health laboratory and expand regional hospitals on atolls with infectious disease wards.

Furthermore, it was noted that other programmes funded by the EU including the “Support to Implement the National Determined Contributions Related to Greenhouse Gas Emissions in the Maldives” (EUR 4.85 million) and the “Prevention of Marine Litter in the Lakshadweep Sea – PROMISE” (EUR 3.7 million) are progressing well.

The meeting took place against a growing concern about the devastating consequences of climate change and extreme weather patterns in Asia and the Pacific, which increasingly put the Maldives and their people especially at risk. Both parties acknowledged the increase of harmful extreme weather patterns, especially in regions that are already particularly vulnerable. They also agreed that the world needs to deepen and accelerate climate action to avoid run-away climate change, while at the same time stepping up climate financing for adaptation to protect people, property, and livelihoods.

The Maldives and the EU reaffirmed their commitment to strengthen the existing cooperation in the multilateral fora. The Maldives emphasized the significant strides made during SIDS4, hosted in Antigua and Barbuda from 27-30 May 2024, including the adoption of the “Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS” unanimously adopted by all Member States, which outlines sustainable development goals for SIDS over the next decade and identifies the support required from the international community to achieve them. The Maldives reaffirmed the confidence in the EU to align assistance to SIDS, with the adopted agenda and continue to be an invaluable partner to the Maldives. The EU and the Maldives will continue joining forces to promote the just and inclusive green transition and support the implementation of global commitments. Both sides will work closely in preparation of the upcoming UN Summit of the Future. Likewise, they reaffirmed commitment to work together on promoting human rights in multilateral fora, including through the Human Rights Council.

The Maldives and the EU remain committed to the global fight against Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated (IUU) fishing and will continue their strong bilateral cooperation in this domain. The Maldives and the EU welcomed the results achieved during the 28th session of the Indian Ocean Tuna Commission (IOTC), and discussed the need to continue joining forces to ensure the sustainable management of fish stocks in the Indian Ocean.

The two sides noted the critical importance of security in the region and the important role that Maldives plays due to its geographic location. The Maldives and the EU explored avenues to further enhance the ongoing security cooperation, including the maritime security domain with the active participation of Maldives in the EU funded Critical Maritime Routes Indo-Pacific (CRIMARIO) that offers to countries IORIS – a secure platform for communication and coordination at the national and regional level, with satellite data, thus strengthening maritime domain awareness and allowing for coordinated responses to incidents. Another area of ongoing security cooperation is the EU funded UNODC implemented project “Support to addressing the risk of terrorism and to increasing security in the Maldives”.

Bolstering the people-to-people ties has been an important call from both sides, with the Maldives restating its request for visa free travel for Maldivian nationals to EU member states. The EU informed that the Maldives’ request for visa-free travel would be addressed when the next review of visa lists takes place. The Maldives welcomed the decision taken by the Council of the European Union in November 2023 to initiate the digitalization of the Schengen Visa procedure, noting that it would ease the visa process and make it more accessible and cost effective for Maldivians.

The Fifth Senior Officials Meeting between the Maldives and EU was co-chaired by Fathimath Inaya, Foreign Secretary, and Paola Pampaloni, Deputy Managing Director for Asia and Pacific at the European External Action Service.

en.title: Foreign Minister Zameer meets the Deputy Managing Director of the European External Actions Service, Ms. Paola Pampaloni
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs Moosa Zameer met Deputy Managing Director of the Asia and Pacific Department of the European External Action Service Paola Pampaloni today.
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs Moosa Zameer met Deputy Managing Director of the Asia and Pacific Department of the European External Action Service Paola Pampaloni today.

The meeting was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and began with Minister Zameer and Deputy Managing Director Pamapaloni reflecting on the significant developments that have been brought forward through the cooperation between the Maldives and the European Union. In recent years, the Maldives has seen significant progress in climate change resilience, judicial reform, and counterterrorism as a direct result of collaboration with the EU.

Minister Zameer expressed his gratitude to the EU for the comprehensive support initiatives offered for the country’s economy and contributions for climate resilient socioeconomic development in the Maldives. This includes the Financing Agreement signed today that allocates €6.5 million of funds that would be channeled to strengthen the blue economy of Maldives. Minister Zameer further highlighted the interest of the Government of Maldives in being included in the list of countries exempt from Schengen visa requirements.

Minister Zameer was accompanied at the meeting by Foreign Secretary Fathimath Inaya, Secretary Bilateral Dr. Hala Hameed, Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed, Senior Under Secretary Hassan Hussain Shihab, Senior Political Director Ahmed Haanee Naeem and Chief Desk Officer, Aminath Shaistha Hamdan Zaki.

Deputy Managing Director Paola Pampaloni is visiting the Maldives to co-chair the Fifth Maldives – European Union Senior Officials Meeting.

ENDS

dv.title: ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު އަލްފާޟިލް މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ޔޫރަޕިއަން އެކްސްޓާނަލް އެކްޝަންސް ސަރވިސް ގެ ޑެޕިއުޓީ މެނޭޖިންގ ޑިރެކްޓަރ މިސް ޕައުލާ ޕަމްޕަލޯނީ އާ ބައްދަލުކުރައްވައިފި
dv.description: ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ޔޫރަޕިއަން އެކްސްޓާނަލް އެކްޝަންސް ސަރވިސް ގެ ޑެޕިއުޓީ މެނޭޖިންގ ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޕައޯލާ ޕަމްޕަލޯނީ އާ މިއަދު ބައްދަލުކުރައްވައިފިއެވެ.
dv.body:
ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ޔޫރަޕިއަން އެކްސްޓާނަލް އެކްޝަންސް ސަރވިސް ގެ ޑެޕިއުޓީ މެނޭޖިންގ ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޕައޯލާ ޕަމްޕަލޯނީ އާ މިއަދު ބައްދަލުކުރައްވައިފިއެވެ.

ޚާރިޖީ ވުޒާރާގައި ބޭއްވުނު މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ވިލާތުގެ އިއްތިހާދާ ދެމެދު އޮންނަ ގުޅުމަށް ލިބިފައިވާ ގިނަގުނަ ކުރިއެރުންތައް ފާހަގަކުރެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި ޚާއްސަކޮށް މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކާއި ގުޅިގެން ދިމާވެފައިވާ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކުން އަރައިގަތުމަށްކުރެވޭ މަސައްކަތްތަކާއި، ޝަރުޢީ ނިޒާމު ހަރުދަނާކުރުމާއި، ނިރުބަވެރިކަމާއި ދެކޮޅަށް ޔޫރަޕުގެ އިއްތިހާދާ ގުޅިގެން ކުރެވޭ މަސައްކަތަކަށް ލިބިފައިވާ ކުރިއެރުންތަކަށްވެސް މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި އަލިއަޅުވާލެވިފައިވެއެވެ.

މިނިސްޓަރ ޒަމީރު ވަނީ ރާއްޖޭގެ އިޤްތިޞާދަށް ވިލާތުގެ އިއްތިހާދުން ފުޅާ ދާއިރާއެއްގައި ވެދެއްވަމުން ގެންދަވާ އެހީތެރިކަމާއި، ރާއްޖޭގެ މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކުގެ ސަބަބުން ރާއްޖޭގެ އިޤްތިޞާދީ އަދި އިޖްތިމާޢީ ކުރިއެރުމަށް އީޔޫއިން ވެދެއްވަމުން ގެންދަވާ އެހީތެރިކަން ފާހަގަކުރައްވައި ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވާފައެވެ. މި މޭރުމުން ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުން، މިނިސްޓަރ ޒަމީރުވަނީ ރާއްޖޭގެ ނޫ އިގްތިސާދު ހަރުދަނާ ކުރުމަށް މަގުފަހިކުރުމަށްޓަކައި ވިލާތުގެ އިއްތިހާދުން ދެއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ 6.5 މިލިއަން ޔޫރޯގެ ފައިނޭންސިން އެގްރީމެންޓްގައި މިއަދު ސޮއިކުރިކުރުން ފާހަގަކުރައްވާފައެވެ. މިނިސްޓަރު ޒަމީރު އިތުރަށް ވިދާޅުވީ ޝެންގެން ވިސާގެ ޝަރުތުތަކުން އިސްތިސްނާވާ ގައުމުތަކުގެ ލިސްޓުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ހިމެނުމަށް ސަރުކާރުން އެދިވަޑައިގަންނަވާކަމަށެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި މިނިސްޓަރ ޒަމީރުގެ އަރިހުގައި ފޮރިން ސެކްރެޓަރީ ފާތިމަތު އިނާޔާ، ސެކްރެޓަރީ ބައިލެޓަރަލް ޑރ. ހާލާ ހަމީދު، ސެކްރެޓަރީ ޝިއުނީން ރަޝީދު، ސީނިއަރ އަންޑަރ ސެކްރެޓަރީ ޙަސަން ޙުސެއިން ޝިހާބް، ސީނިއަރ ޕޮލިޓިކަލް ޑިރެކްޓަރ އަލްފާޟިލް އަޙްމަދު ހާނީ ނަޢީމް އާއި ޗީފް ޑެސްކް އޮފިސަރ އާމިނަތު ޝައިސްތާ ހަމްދާން ޒަކީ ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގެންނެވިއެވެ.

ފޮރިން ސެކްރެޓަރީ ފާތިމަތު އިނާޔާ އަދި ޑެޕިއުޓީ މެނޭޖިންގ ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޕައުލާ ޕަމްޕަލޯނީ ކޯޗެއަރ ކުރައްވާގޮތަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ވިލާތުގެ އިއްތިހާދާ ދެމެދު ބޭއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ ފަސް ވަނީ އިސްވެރިންގެ ބައްދަލުވުން މިއަދު މެންދުރު ޚާރިޖީ ވުޒާރާގައި ބޭއްވުނެވެ.

ނިމުނީ.

en.title: Minister Zameer sends Republic Day greetings to the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Italy
en.description: Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends Republic Day greetings to Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the Republic of Italy, Antonio Tajani.
en.body:
Minister for Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends Republic Day greetings to Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the Republic of Italy, Antonio Tajani.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Maldives, I take great pleasure in offering my warm greetings and felicitations to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Italy on the occasion of the Republic Day of Italy.

With over 50 years of diplomatic relations, the Maldives recognizes Italy as an enduring partner in development and collaboration. I look forward to working closely to continue to foster even closer relations and bring about positive initiatives of mutual benefit.

Please accept, Excellency, my best wishes for your health and the prosperity of your people, as well as the assurances of my highest considerations.”

ENDS

dv.title: އިޓަލީގެ ބޮޑުވަޒީރުގެ ނައިބު އަދި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށް ޖުމްހޫރީ ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ފޮނުއްވައިފި
dv.description: އިޓަލީގެ ޤައުމީ ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ބޮޑު ވަޒީރުގެ ނައިބު އަދި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު އެންޓޯނިއޯ ޓަޖާނީ އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފި އެވެ.
dv.body:
އިޓަލީގެ ޤައުމީ ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ބޮޑު ވަޒީރުގެ ނައިބު އަދި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު އެންޓޯނިއޯ ޓަޖާނީ އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފި އެވެ.

މިނިސްޓަރުގެ މެސެޖު ތިރީގައި މިވަނީއެވެ.

"ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ނަމުގައި، އިޓަލީގެ ޖުމްހޫރީ ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި މަނިކުފާނަށާއި އިޓަލީގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް  އިޚްލާސްތެރި ތަހުނިޔާ އާއި ހެޔޮ އެދުންތައް ފޮނުވަމަކީ އަޅުގަނޑަށް ލިބޭ ވަރަށް ބޮޑު އުފަލެކެވެ.
ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި އިޓަލީ އާ ދެމެދު ޚާރިޖީ ގުޅުން ގާއިމުކުރެވުނުފަހުން 50 އަހަރަށް ވުރެ ގިނަ ދުވަސް ވެފައިވާއިރު، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ދެކެނީ އިޓަލީއަކީ ތަރައްޤީގެ މުހިންމު ބައިވެރިއެއްގެ ގޮތުގައެވެ. އަޅުގަނޑުގެ އުއްމީދަކީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި އިޓަލީ އާ ދެމެދު އޮންނަ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިވެ، ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައި ފައިދާހުރި ރަނގަޅު މަސައްކަތްތައް ކުރިޔަށް ގެންދިޔުމެވެ.
މަނިކުފާނަށް ދުޅަހެޔޮ ސިއްޙަތާއި އިޓަލީގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ސުލްހަ އާއި ތަނަވަސްކަން އިތުރު ވުމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު އެދެމެވެ.
އަޅުގަނޑު މަނިކުފާނަށް ކުރާ މަތިވެރި ޤަދަރު އާކޮށް، އެކަން ޔަޤީންކޮށް އެރުވުމަށް، މި ފުރުސަތުގެ ބޭނުންކުރީމެވެ."

en.title: Maldives to host the “Fifth Maldives – European Union Senior Officials Meeting”
en.description: The Fifth Maldives – European Union (EU) Senior Officials Meeting will take place tomorrow, 2 June 2024, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives. The purpose of the meeting is to have open and constructive dialogue between the Maldives and EU, aiming to build upon existing…
en.body:
The Fifth Maldives – European Union (EU) Senior Officials Meeting will take place tomorrow, 2 June 2024, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives.  The purpose of the meeting is to have open and constructive dialogue between the Maldives and EU, aiming to build upon existing bonds of friendship and collaboration.

This year’s meeting will focus on issues pertaining to enhanced collaboration on democratic reforms, green transition, climate change mitigation and adaptation, good governance, judiciary reforms and security, as well as examining the outcomes of existing initiatives to determine further cooperation.

The Maldives delegation will be led by Foreign Secretary, Fathimath Inaya. The meeting will be attended by senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the President’s Office, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Economic Development and Trade, Ministry of Fisheries and Ocean Resources, Attorney General’s Office, Ministry of Climate Change, Environment and Energy, National Counter Terrorism Center, MNDF Coast Guard Maldives Police Service and the National Reintegration Center.

The delegation from the European Union will be led by Paola Pampaloni, Deputy Managing Director of the Asia and Pacific Department of the European External Action Service.

ENDS.

dv.title: ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ވިލާތުގެ އިއްތިހާދާ ދެމެދު ބޭއްވޭ 5 ވަނަ މޯލްޑިވްސް – އީ.ޔޫ ސީނިއަރ އޮފިޝަލުންގެ ބައްދަލުވުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގައި ބާއްވަނީ
dv.description: ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ވިލާތުގެ އިއްތިހާދާ ދެމެދު ބޭއްވޭ 5 ވަނަ ސީނިއަރ އޮފިޝަލުންގެ ބައްދަލުވުން މާދަމާ ޚާރިޖީ ވުޒާރާގައި ބޭއްވުމަށްވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގެ މައިގަނޑު މަޤުޞަދަކީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ވިލާތުގެ އިއްތިހާދާ ދެމެދު ބިނާކުރަނިވި މަޝްވާރަތަށް ކުރިއަށް ގެންގޮސް، ދެ ފަރާތުގެ ދެމެދުގައި…
dv.body:
ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ވިލާތުގެ އިއްތިހާދާ ދެމެދު ބޭއްވޭ 5 ވަނަ ސީނިއަރ އޮފިޝަލުންގެ ބައްދަލުވުން މާދަމާ ޚާރިޖީ ވުޒާރާގައި ބޭއްވުމަށްވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގެ މައިގަނޑު މަޤުޞަދަކީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ވިލާތުގެ އިއްތިހާދާ ދެމެދު ބިނާކުރަނިވި މަޝްވާރަތަށް ކުރިއަށް ގެންގޮސް، ދެ ފަރާތުގެ ދެމެދުގައި މިހާރު އޮތް ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިކުރުމެވެ.

މި އަހަރުގެ ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ޑިމޮކްރަސީ ހަރުދަނާ ކުރުމާއި، ތިމާވެއްޓާއި ރައްޓެހި ތަރައްޤީ ކުރިއަރުވައި، މޫސުމަށް އަންނަ ބަދަލުތަކުން ދިމާވާ ގޮންޖެހުންތަކުން އަރައިގަތުމަށް ކުރެވޭ މަސައްކަތްތަކުގައި އެއްބާރުލުން ދިނުމާއި، ހެޔޮވެރިކަން ކުރިއަރުވައި، ޝަރުޢީ ދާއިރާ ކުރިއެރުވުމުގެ އިތުރުން ސަލާމަތީ ދާއިރާއިން ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާ ކުރުމަށް ކުރެވިދާނެ ކަންކަމާއި ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކުރުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވެއެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ވަފުދުގެ އިސްވެރިއަކަށް ހުންނަވާނީ ފޮރިން ސެކްރެޓަރީ ފާތިމަތު އިނާޔާއެވެ. މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާގެ އޮފީސް، މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް، މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފިނޭންސް، މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް އިކޮނޮމިކް ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓް އެންޑް ޓްރޭޑް، މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފިޝަރީޒް އެންޑް އޯޝަން ރިސޯސަސް، އެޓަރނީ ޖެނެރަލްގެ އޮފީސް، މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ކްލައިމެޓް ޗޭންޖް، އެންވަޔަރަންމަންޓް އެންޑް އެނާރޖީ، ނޭޝަނަލް ކައުންޓަރ ޓެރަރިޒަމް ސެންޓަރު، އެމް.އެން.ޑީ.އެފް ކޯސްޓް ގާޑު، ދިވެހި ފުލުހުންގެ ޚިދުމަތް އަދި ނޭޝަނަލް ރީއިންޓަގްރޭޝަން ސެންޓަރުގެ އިސް ބޭފުޅުން ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަތުމަށްވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ.

ވިލާތުގެ އިއްތިހާދުގެ ވަފުދުގެ އިސްވެރިއަކަށް ހުންނަވާނީ ޔޫރަޕިއަން އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެކްޝަން ސަރވިސްގެ އޭޝިއާ އެންޑް ޕެސިފިކް ޑިޕާރޓްމަންޓްގެ ޑެޕިއުޓީ މެނޭޖިންގ ޑިރެކްޓަރ ޕައޯލާ ޕަމްޕަލޯނީއެވެ.

ނިމުނީ

en.title: Minister Zameer sends Independence Day greetings to the Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Samoa
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends message of felicitations to Fiamē Naomi Mata'afa, Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Independent State of Samoa, on the occasion of their Independence Day.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer sends message of felicitations to Fiamē Naomi Mata'afa, Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Independent State of Samoa, on the occasion of their Independence Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It gives me great pleasure to convey warm greetings and sincere good wishes of the Government and the people of the Maldives, and on my own behalf, to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of Samoa, on your Independence Day.

As we gear up for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Apia later this year, I remain confident in Samoa’s able leadership to drive the agenda on issues of mutual concern and on shared priorities. I am also confident that the relations between the Maldives and Samoa will continue to prosper and flourish in the years to come.

Let me extend my best wishes for Your Excellency’s good health and well-being, and for further peace and prosperity for the people of Samoa.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest considerations.”

ENDS

dv.title: ‎ސަމޯއާގެ ބޮޑު ވަޒީރު އަދި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރަށް އެ ގައުމުގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ފޮނުއްވައިފި
dv.description: ‎ސަމޯއާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ބޮޑު ވަޒީރު އަދި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ފިއާމޭ ނައޯމީ މަޓައާފާ އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފި އެވެ.
dv.body:
‎ސަމޯއާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ބޮޑު ވަޒީރު އަދި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، ފިއާމޭ ނައޯމީ މަޓައާފާ އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު، މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ތަހުނިޔާގެ މެސެޖެއް ފޮނުއްވައިފި އެވެ.

‎މިނިސްޓަރުގެ މެސެޖު ތިރީގައި މިވަނީއެވެ.

‎"ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ނަމުގައި، އަދި އަޅުގަނޑުގެ އަމިއްލަ ނަމުގައި، ސަމޯއާގެ މިނިވަން ދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިޔާ އާއި އިޚްލާޞްތެރި ހެޔޮއެދުންތައް، ކަމަނާ އާއި ސަމޯއާ ސަރުކާރު އަދި އެންމެހާ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ފޮނުވުމަކީ އަޅުގަނޑަށް ލިބޭ ވަރަށް ބޮޑު އުފަލެކެވެ.

‎މިއަހަރުގެ ފަހުކޮޅު އަޕިއާގައި ބާއްވާ 'ކޮމަންވެލްތު ހެޑްސް އޮފް ގަވަރމަންޓް މީޓިންގ' އަށް ތައްޔާރުވަމުންދާއިރު، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ އާއި ސަމޯއާ އިން ކަންބޮޑުވާ މައްސަލަތަކާއި ދެޤައުމުން އިސްކަންދޭ ކަންކަމަށް މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގެ ތެރެއިން އެދެވޭ ހައްލުތަކެއް ހޯދުމަށް ސަމޯއާ އިން ކެނޑިނޭޅި މަސައްކަތް ކުރާނެކަން އަޅުގަނޑަށް ޔަގީނެވެ. އަދި ކުރިއަށް އޮތް އަހަރުތަކުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ އާއި ސަމޯއާގެ ގުޅުން ކުރިއަރާ، އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިވެގެންދާނެކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަންވެސް އަޅުގަނޑަށް އެބައޮތެވެ.

‎ކަމަނާ އަށް ދުޅަހެޔޮ ސިއްޙަތާއި ސަމޯއާ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ސުލްހައާއި ތަނަވަސްކަން ލިބުމަށް އަޅުގަނޑު އެދެމެވެ.

‎އަޅުގަނޑު ކަމަނާއަށް ކުރާ މަތިވެރި ޤަދަރު އާކޮށް، އެކަން ޔަޤީންކޮށް އެރުވުމަށް، މި ފުރުސަތުގެ ބޭނުންކުރީމެވެ.

ނިމުނީ

en.title: The Minister of Foreign Affairs His Excellency Moosa Zameer to undertake an Official Visit to Sri Lanka from 3 to 6 June 2024
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Moosa Zameer will undertake an Official visit to Colombo, Sri Lanka at the invitation of His Excellency M.U.M. Ali Sabry, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka from 3 – 6 June 2024.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs, His Excellency Moosa Zameer will undertake an Official visit to Colombo, Sri Lanka  at the invitation of His Excellency M.U.M. Ali Sabry, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka from 3 – 6 June 2024.

During the visit, Foreign Minister Zameer is scheduled to pay courtesy calls on His Excellency Ranil Wickremesinghe, President of Sri Lanka and His Excellency, Dinesh Gunawardena, Prime Minister of Sri Lanka. Minister Zameer will also hold bilateral talks with His Excellency M.U.M. Ali Sabry, Minister of Foreign Affairs, and explore avenues to further strengthening the longstanding bilateral relations between the two countries. In addition to this, the meeting will discuss the provision of convenient facilities to the Maldivians residing in Sri Lanka.

Minister Zameer will be accompanied by Her Excellency Sheryna Abdul Samad, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency, Shiruzimath Sameer, Additional Secretary and Ms. Aishath Fareena, Director General at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

ENDS

dv.title: މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް މޫސާ ޒަމީރު، އަންނަ ޖޫން މަހުގެ 3 އިން 6 އަށް ސްރީލަންކާގެ ވެރިރަށް ކޮލޮމްބޯއަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށްވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ
dv.description: އަންނަ ޖޫން މަހުގެ 3 އިން 6 އަށް މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް މޫސާ ޒަމީރު، ސްރީލަންކާގެ ވެރިރަށް ކޮލޮމްބޯއަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށްވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. މި ދަތުރުފުޅަކީ ސްރީލަންކާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ހިސް އެކްސެލަންސީ އެމް.ޔޫ.އެމް. ޢަލީ ސަބްރީގެ ދަޢުވަތަކަށް ކުރައްވާ ރަސްމީ…
dv.body:
އަންނަ ޖޫން މަހުގެ 3 އިން 6 އަށް މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް މޫސާ ޒަމީރު، ސްރީލަންކާގެ ވެރިރަށް ކޮލޮމްބޯއަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށްވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. މި ދަތުރުފުޅަކީ ސްރީލަންކާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ހިސް އެކްސެލަންސީ އެމް.ޔޫ.އެމް. ޢަލީ ސަބްރީގެ ދަޢުވަތަކަށް ކުރައްވާ ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެކެވެ.

އެ މަނިކުފާނުގެ މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އެ ޤައުމުގެ ސަރުކާރުގެ އިސް ބޭފުޅުންނާއި ބައްދަލު ކުރެއްވުމަށްވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. އޭގެތެރޭގައި އެޤައުމުގެ ރައީސް، ހިސް އެކްސަލަންސީ ރަނިލް ވިކްރަމަސިންގްހެ އާއި ބޮޑުވަޒީރު، ހިސް އެކްސަލަންސީ ޑިނޭޝް ގުނަވަރދެނާ ހިމެނެއެވެ. އަދި އެ ޤައުމުގެ ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރާ ބައްދަލުކުރައްވާ ރަސްމީ ވާހަކަތައް ދެއްކުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވެއެވެ. ރަސްމީ ވާހަކަތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ސްރީލަންކާއާއި ދެމެދު އޮތް ޒަމާންވީ ގުޅުން ހަރުދަނާ ކުރުމުގެ މަޝްވަރާތައް ކުރިއަށްދާނެއެވެ. އަދި މީގެ އިތުރުން ސްރީލަންކާގައި ދިރިއުޅޭ ދިވެހި ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ލުއިފަސޭހަ ގޮތްތައް ހޯދާ ދިނުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކުރުމަށްވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ.

ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ މޫސާ ޒަމީރު ސްރީލަންކާއަށް ކުރައްވާ މި ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅަކީ، އެ މަނިކުފާނު މިނިސްޓަރ ކަމުގެ މަޤާމާ ހަވާލުވެވަޑައިގަތުމަށްފަހު ސްރީލަންކާއަށް ކުރައްވާ ފުރަތަމަ ދަތުރުފުޅެވެ.

en.title: Minister Zameer calls for stronger public-private partnerships to drive transformational change in SIDS
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Moosa Zameer, today delivered remarks at the Private Sector Roundtable during the Fourth International Conference on Small Island Developing States (SIDS) held in Antigua and Barbuda.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Moosa Zameer, today delivered remarks at the Private Sector Roundtable during the Fourth International Conference on Small Island Developing States (SIDS) held in Antigua and Barbuda.

In his address, Foreign Minister Zameer described public-private partnerships as a compelling framework for collaboration, as they involve pooling together resources and expertise, reducing risk significantly. He stated that through genuine partnerships, governments and businesses can deliver essential services and develop infrastructure in various sectors including healthcare, education, transportation, and energy.

Drawing on his experience in the private sector, Minister Zameer urged the private sector to engage more actively with SIDS. He noted that private sector investment has the potential to catalyse transformative change. He called on governments to create an enabling environment for businesses to invest in SIDS, through robust policies and economic diversification. He also called on the international community to support boosting the state and productive capacities of SIDS, which would enable SIDS to mobilise resources and attract investment.

The Private Sector Roundtable, organized by the United Nations Office of the High Representative for the Least Developed Countries, Landlocked Developing Countries and Small Island Developing States (UN OHRLLS), gathered leaders from governments, the private sector and civil society to discuss the importance of partnerships towards the implementation of the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS. The Roundtable also showcased the outcomes of the SIDS Global Business Network Forum, which was held from 25-26 May 2024.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Zameer sends Republic Day greetings to the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Nepal
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Moosa Zameer has sent a message of felicitations to the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Nepal, His Excellency Narayan Kaji Shrestha, on the occasion of Nepal’s Republic Day.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Moosa Zameer has sent a message of felicitations to the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Nepal, His Excellency Narayan Kaji Shrestha, on the occasion of Nepal’s Republic Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and the people of Maldives, I extend warm felicitations to Your Excellency and the people of Nepal on the auspicious occasion of the Republic Day of Nepal.

I am confident that the strong and mutually beneficial ties that exist between Maldives and Nepal will grow and strengthen in the years to come. I look forward to working closely with Your Excellency in enhancing friendship between our two peoples and promoting cooperation in various fields.

I wish Your Excellency, good health, and continued success in your endeavor to bring growth and prosperity to Nepal.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

ENDS

en.title: Minister Zameer sends Independence Day greetings to Azerbaijan
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Moosa Zameer sends warm felicitations to His Excellency Jeyhun Bayramov, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Azerbaijan on the occasion of Azerbaijan’s Independence Day.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Moosa Zameer sends warm felicitations to His Excellency Jeyhun Bayramov, Minister for Foreign Affairs of Azerbaijan on the occasion of Azerbaijan’s Independence Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On this joyous occasion of Azerbaijan’s Independence Day, it gives me great pleasure to extend warm felicitations and sincere good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the people of Azerbaijan.

I look forward to working closely with your Excellency, both bilaterally and on international issues of mutual concern to bolster the good relations that exist between our two countries.

Let me also take this opportunity to extend my best wishes for Your Excellency’s good health and success, and for the continued peace, progress and prosperity of the people of Azerbaijan.   Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration”.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Zameer sends a message of condolence to the Foreign Minister of France
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer, sends a message of condolence to Stéphane Séjourné, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer, sends a message of condolence to Stéphane Séjourné, Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs of France

The Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On behalf of the Government and the people of the Republic of Maldives, I convey our profound sadness following the untimely demise of Ambassador Jean-François Pactet, the Ambassador of France to the Maldives.

Ambassador Pactet will be remembered as a dear friend of the Maldives, who tirelessly worked to strengthen the robust relations between the Maldives and France. My thoughts and prayers are with the Ambassador’s family and loved ones. I extend my sincere condolences to all members of the French Embassy in Colombo, and to the French diplomatic service.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration”.

ENDS

en.title: Minister Zameer sends a message of condolence to the Foreign Minister of Papua New Guinea
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer, sends a message of condolence to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Independent State of Papua New Guinea, Justin Tkatchenko, following the devastating landslide in Papua New Guinea.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, Moosa Zameer, sends a message of condolence to the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Independent State of Papua New Guinea, Justin Tkatchenko, following the devastating landslide in Papua New Guinea.

The Minister’s message reads as follows:

“I am deeply saddened to hear the news of the devastating landslide in Papua New Guinea, which has resulted in the loss of hundreds of lives and widespread destruction.

On behalf of the Government and people of the Maldives, and on my own behalf, I extend my sincere condolences to the Government and people of Papua New Guinea and all those affected by this tragic disaster.

We hope the rescue operations currently underway are successful in mitigating as much loss of life as possible.”

ENDS
